slides.title: Words in a list
slides.text:
Sometimes we list things we do:

I **run**, **jump** and **swim**.

All three words are the **same kind** of word. That makes the sentence easy to read.

slides.title: Make them match
slides.text:
Right: I like **reading**, **drawing** and **singing**.
Wrong: I like reading, drawing and to sing.

If the first word ends in **-ing**, the others do too.

slides.title: Match across sentences
slides.text:
Steps in a list should match too.

**Wash** your hands.
**Dry** them well.
**Sit** down to eat.

Each step starts with an action word.

proof.title: Prove it from the text
proof.text:
1. Find the other items in the list.
2. Look at **how they start** or **how they end**.
3. Your answer must have the **same form**.

The matching sentences in the text prove your answer.

example.explain:
Each sentence starts with **She** and an action word: sweeps, waters, feeds.

They all match. That is **parallel structure**.

together.passage: Our class made a plan to keep the school clean. First, we will pick up litter. Next, we will recycle paper. Last, we will ___.
together.hint: Look at the other steps. What words come after **we will**?
together.good: Yes! **pick up**, **recycle**, **plant**: all three steps match.

sentences: Our class made a plan to keep the school clean.
First, we will pick up litter.
Next, we will recycle paper.
Last, we will ___.
evidence.stem: The answer was: plant trees. Tap 2 sentences that show the pattern the answer must match.
evidence.wrong: This sentence is not one of the steps. Find the steps that start with 'we will'.

checks.passage: At the park, the children ran, jumped and ___.
checks.why: **ran**, **jumped**, **climbed**: all three tell what they did in the past.

checks.passage: Mom said, "Brush your teeth. Put on your pyjamas. You should read a book."
checks.why: The other steps start with an action word. It should be: **Read a book.**

again.title: Listen for the beat
again.text:
Say the list out loud. Matching words sound like a **drum beat**.

If one word sounds different, change it to match the others.
again.example:
I like to sing, to draw and dancing.

**to sing**, **to draw**, ... dancing? It breaks the beat. Fix it: **to dance**.

slides.title: Parallel structure
slides.text:
**Parallel** means the parts of a list or pair have the **same form**.

Nouns go with nouns. Verbs go with verbs. Describing words go with describing words.

slides.title: Check the tense
slides.text:
Verbs in a list should be in the **same tense**.

Right: Ali **washed** the car and **cleaned** the windows.
Wrong: Ali washed the car and cleans the windows.

slides.title: Pairs with and / or
slides.text:
Words joined by **and** or **or** should match.

Right: The soup was **hot** and **tasty**.
Wrong: The soup was hot and had a good taste.

proof.title: Prove it from the text
proof.text:
1. Find the items that go together.
2. Name their form: action word? noun? -ing word? past tense?
3. Pick the answer with the **same form**.

Point to the matching items in the text. They are your proof.

sentences.t: Our teacher gave us three tips for the test.
Check your work at the end.

example.explain:
Each tip starts with a command word: **Read**, **Answer**, **Check**.

The tips are parallel, so they are easy to follow.

together.passage: Before our trip to the wildlife park, our teacher gave us three rules. Stay with your group. Listen to the guide. ___. At the park, we saw giraffes, zebras and a sleepy lion. It was the best trip of the year.
together.stem: Which sentence best fills the blank?
options: Feeding the animals is not allowed.
You shouldn't be feeding the animals.
together.hint: How do the other two rules begin? Your rule should begin the same way.
together.good: Yes! **Stay**, **Listen**, **Do not feed**: each rule is a command.

sentences: Before our trip to the wildlife park, our teacher gave us three rules.
Stay with your group.
Listen to the guide.
At the park, we saw giraffes, zebras and a sleepy lion.
It was the best trip of the year.
evidence.stem: The answer was: Do not feed the animals. Tap 2 sentences that show the form the rule must match.
evidence.wrong: This sentence is not one of the rules. Find the rules that start with a command word.

checks.passage: The new library is bright, quiet and ___.
Last night, Huda finished her homework and ___ her bag for school.
checks.why: **finished** is past tense, so the second verb must be past too: **packed**.

checks.passage: Our coach wants us to eat well, sleep early and drinking water.
checks.stem: Which change makes the sentence parallel?
checks.why: **eat**, **sleep**, **drink**: all three must be the same form.

again.title: Line them up
again.text: Write the items **one under the other**. Then look at how each one starts.
again.example:
Dad likes to cook, to garden and fixing bikes.

to cook
to garden
fixing bikes  ✘

Fix: **to fix bikes**.

slides.title: Phrases in parallel
slides.text:
Parallel structure works for **phrases**, not just single words.

We came **to learn**, **to share** and **to have fun**.
She ran **across the yard**, **through the gate** and **down the street**.

slides.title: Paired words
slides.text:
Some joining words come in **pairs**:

**both … and**
**either … or**
**neither … nor**
**not only … but also**

What comes after the first word must match what comes after the second.

slides.title: Fixing a paired sentence
slides.text:
Wrong: She is **not only** a good student **but also** plays football well.

Right: She is **not only** a good **student** **but also** a skilled **player**.

Now both parts are nouns.

proof.title: Prove it from the text
proof.text:
1. Find the joining word: and, or, both, either, not only.
2. Look at the part **before** the blank or the first item.
3. Choose the answer with the same form.

Other lists and pairs in the passage show how the writer keeps things parallel.

sentences.t: Desert plants survive in two clever ways.
They either store water in thick leaves or send long roots deep underground.
Because of this, they are both tough and useful to animals.

example.explain:
**either store … or send**: two verbs.
**both tough and useful**: two describing words.

Each pair matches, so the writing is parallel.

together.passage: Every spring, students at our school run a book fair. The fair has two goals: to raise money for the library and to get students excited about reading. Volunteers can either sell books at the tables or ___. Last year, the fair was both busy and successful. Next year, the organisers hope to invite an author, to add a story corner and to stay open longer.
options: to help children choosing a book
together.hint: Look at the words after **either**: sell books. The words after **or** must have the same form.
together.good: Yes! **either sell … or help**: both parts start with a plain action word.

sentences: Every spring, students at our school run a book fair.
The fair has two goals: to raise money for the library and to get students excited about reading.
Volunteers can either sell books at the tables or ___.
Last year, the fair was both busy and successful.
Next year, the organisers hope to invite an author, to add a story corner and to stay open longer.
evidence.stem: The answer was: help children choose a book. Tap 2 OTHER sentences with a complete pair or list in the same form.
evidence.wrong: This sentence does not have a complete matching pair or list. Find one where every part has the same form.

checks.passage: For the science fair, we must choose a question, plan an experiment and ___.
checks.why: **choose**, **plan**, **record**: each item starts with an action word.

checks.passage: Mangroves protect the coast not only by holding the mud in place but also ___.
checks.why: **by holding** … **by slowing**: both parts after the paired words match.

checks.passage: Faris spent the holiday visiting his cousins, reading adventure stories and he learned to swim.
checks.stem: Which is the best way to rewrite the end?

again.title: Cover and check
again.text: Cover the joining word and read each part **on its own** after the start of the sentence. Each part should work.
again.example:
The trip was both fun and taught us a lot.

'The trip was fun' ✔
'The trip was taught us a lot' ✘

Fix: The trip was both **fun** and **educational**.

slides.title: Parallel clauses
slides.text:
Whole **clauses** can be parallel too.

The scientists hoped **that** the reef would recover **and that** the fish would return.

Repeat the starting word (that, because, when) so each clause begins the same way.

slides.title: Comparisons
slides.text:
When you compare two things, put them in the **same form**.

Wrong: Walking to school is healthier than to ride in a car.
Right: **Walking** to school is healthier than **riding** in a car.

slides.title: Why writers use it
slides.text:
Parallel structure gives writing **rhythm** and **balance**. Speakers use it to make ideas memorable:

'We will plan carefully, work honestly and finish proudly.'

Breaking the pattern makes a reader stumble.

proof.title: Prove it from the text
proof.text:
1. Find the items being joined or compared.
2. Identify their exact form: clause, -ing phrase, to-phrase, noun phrase.
3. Choose the option that copies that form.

Look at other balanced sentences in the passage. A careful writer keeps the same pattern throughout.

sentences.t: Learning a new language is like building a house.
You lay the foundation with simple words, raise the walls with grammar, and finish the rooms with practice.
Rushing the work is riskier than taking your time.

example.explain:
**lay**, **raise**, **finish**: three matching verb phrases build the comparison.

**Rushing** … **taking**: the two things compared are both -ing forms.

together.passage: When a coral reef in the Red Sea was damaged by a ship, a team of marine scientists began a long repair project. Diving to the reef was harder than they had expected but safer than they had feared. They planted young corals on metal frames, cleaned away broken rubble and measured the water temperature every week. They hoped that the corals would grow, that the fish would return and that ___. Three years later, small schools of fish were swimming among new branches of coral. Today, visitors can see the results for themselves.
together.stem: Which words best fill the blank?
options: for the water to stay clean
together.hint: The two items before it both start with **that** and follow with a subject and **would**. Copy that pattern.
together.good: Yes! **that the corals would grow**, **that the fish would return**, **that the water would stay clean**: three matching clauses.

sentences: When a coral reef in the Red Sea was damaged by a ship, a team of marine scientists began a long repair project.
Diving to the reef was harder than they had expected but safer than they had feared.
They planted young corals on metal frames, cleaned away broken rubble and measured the water temperature every week.
They hoped that the corals would grow, that the fish would return and that ___.
Three years later, small schools of fish were swimming among new branches of coral.
Today, visitors can see the results for themselves.
evidence.stem: The answer was: the water would stay clean. Tap 2 OTHER sentences that also keep their parts parallel.
evidence.wrong: This sentence does not join or compare items in matching forms. Find one with a balanced pair or list.

checks.passage: Our principal said that the new rules would keep students safe, help classes start on time and ___.
checks.stem: Which words best fill the blank?
options: noise in the hallways will reduce
checks.why: **keep**, **help**, **reduce**: each item is a plain verb phrase after **would**.

checks.passage: Many people believe that to read on paper is easier than reading on a screen.
checks.stem: Which change makes the comparison parallel?
options: Change **on a screen** to **with a screen**.
checks.why: **Reading** on paper … **reading** on a screen: both things compared are now -ing forms.

checks.passage: A good leader listens carefully, speaks honestly and ___.
checks.stem: Which words best fill the blank?
checks.why: **listens carefully**, **speaks honestly**, **decides fairly**: verb plus -ly word each time.

again.title: Find the twin
again.text: Every item in a parallel sentence has a **twin**. Find the first item, then make the next one look like it.
again.example:
She came home tired, hungry and wanting to sleep.

Twins: **tired**, **hungry** (describing words). The third should match: **sleepy**.

She came home **tired, hungry and sleepy**.
